note: 505-token AbAg complex, no MSA. The 0.76047 A PASS numerator was recorded on pc (p150a, ttnn 0.68.0) at fixture birth 2026-08-11; on qb1 (p150a, ttnn 0.67.4) the identical commit range 4a89d38d..8c878dd0 measures 6.45-6.71 A, byte-stable per run, identical across cards, including at the fixture commit itself, so no tt-bio code moved the number. The qb1 value also wanders with uncontrolled low-level host state (6.4474 -> 6.71027 across 3.5 h at one fixed commit), so the exact numerator is not a stable gate quantity for this target on a single host. Accuracy adjudication vs experimental ground truth (9ncy.cif): device fold 6.49 A (TM 0.935, lDDT 0.791), CPU bf16 reference 6.43 A (TM 0.924), CPU fp32 reference 6.55 A (TM 0.931) — three equally accurate basins of a low-signal no-MSA target, the device fold not worse than either reference. The envelope numerator measures basin identity on a chaotic no-MSA landscape, which is stack-sensitive, not correctness. Same accepted class as boltz2-prot-nomsa (seed-0 chaotic-trajectory amplification, docs/implementation-parity.md). A live GAP reproduces this committed GAP-evidenced verdict, so the gate does not block on it; a PASS on the pc stack reads as improvement. Reference side (meta.json, ref_bf16/ref_fp32) untouched. ttnn version is NOT the variable: on qb1 the identical tree measures numerator 6.71027497819683 and envelope 1.6594001346777516 under ttnn 0.67.4 and under the pinned ttnn 0.68.0, bit-identical every digit (tt-bio v0.6.3 release gate, 2026-08-17, same host same cards). The 0.67.4 named above is only which interpreter that run used, not a cause; the pc-vs-qb1 split is host-keyed and still unexplained.
